title: Comparison of Three Minimally Invasive Surgical Approaches for Total Hip Arthroplasty with Regard to Muscle Status on MRI and Functional Outcome.
summary:
Currently, it is unclear which of the three minimally invasive approaches to the hip joint most commonly used in Germany for total hip arthroplasty causes the least muscle damage. Therefore, the question arises as to whether, in a direct comparison of the approaches under conditions that are as identical as possible, a difference in the muscle damage to the hip muscles can be demonstrated.
This can be assessed both through imaging using magnetic resonance imaging and through questionnaires that ask about limitations in daily life caused by the hip.
These examinations and questionnaires are carried out in addition to routine care before the operation as well as three and twelve months after the operation.
conditions: Presence of an artificial hip joint.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned primary unilateral total hip arthroplasty at the Center for Endoprosthetics, Hessing Kliniken Augsburg, due to present coxarthrosis requiring intervention, using the direct anterior, minimally invasive anterolateral, or piriformis-sparing posterior approach.
Exclusion criteria:
Presence of previous surgery in the hip joint area, femoral head necrosis, acute infections, hip dysplasia greater than Crowe grade 1, neuromuscular disorders, or claustrophobia.
